Hey folks,
This one was heavy. **Katie Phang** and I sat down to talk through Epstein, the rot at DOJ, the targeting of journalists, ICE violence, and a measles outbreak that tells you everything about how broken this moment is -- and why people are still showing up anyway.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] Katie opens up about the emotional and physical toll of reporting from Minneapolis after Alex Pretti's murder
* [**00:07:36**] Todd Blanche's Epstein comments -- and why the DOJ's callousness should terrify every parent
* [**00:15:18**] The cover-up problem: who's being protected, who isn't, and why this isn't partisan
* [**00:28:01**] Don Lemon's arrest, independent journalism under attack, and why they're scared of growing voices
* [**00:44:50**] Community, love, and resistance -- why Minnesota reminded us all that hope isn't dead

This conversation spans not only the moral collapse that lets a measles outbreak spread through a detention facility full of kids, but something deeper too: how anger becomes action, why community still matters, and what it means to keep going when the weight of all this feels unbearable. If you value honest, unfiltered conversations like this -- and independent media that refuses to look away -- help me keep them going.

# ["Front-Runner"](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=186790398&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg2NzkwMzk4LCJpYXQiOjE3NzAxNjM2MDksImV4cCI6MTc3Mjc1NTYwOSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.vAznwE_rwSwDplObaSW2mWVRWGdv6dHEM5n_z2pmVdI)
### Gratitude, momentum, and the unsexy work that got us here
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Feb 4
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..qN3j2wA6EwzN37k1TWi8WhdX48KY22Al73imRpy0T1g?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/front-runner?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Yesterday, I was hustling between meetings when my team sent me a clip from _MS NOW_. They said, "You're going to want to see this."
- A senior national political reporter at _Politico_ was talking about Michigan's Senate race when he said something brief, but important.
_**He called me the front-runner.**_
This is big. But it's not about me.
I'm sharing this because of what it represents: Momentum like this doesn't come from one speech, one headline, or one person. It comes from doggedness. From unglamorous work. From showing up for Michiganders again and again, even when the news is chaotic, you're exhausted, and the days feel long.
In other words, it comes from _you_.
This grassroots team has stepped up time and time again. You've pushed me, lifted me, and inspired me to fight every day for Michiganders who want steady leadership - leadership that's focused on getting things done and on using government to actually make working people's lives better.
I'm deeply grateful for your quiet optimism, belief, and strength.
**We 're not the loudest campaign. **We're not the flashiest. We're not the most "viral."**** But we're the front-runner because we're built by hardworking Michiganders - people who are ready for something better.
That's the energy behind this campaign.
So when a national reporter analyzes this race and sees a front-runner, they're talking about all of us. The teachers and nurses. The autoworkers and retirees. The small-business owners and students. The people who are busting their tails every day and deserve someone who will fight for them in the U.S. Senate.
That's what's being recognized.
**The truth is this race is going to be close.** New polling shows we're statistically tied with our MAGA Republican opponent. But moments like this are reminders that the work matters - and that it's adding up.
We're building something real here. Not flashy. Not fueled by billionaires. Built the Michigan way: shoulder to shoulder, steadily, with grit.
And yes,**I believe we can win.**
Not because an analyst said so on TV. But because I know what this grassroots team is capable of.
We're just getting started.
More soon.
With gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/d187cfe1-f75a-4002-b26e-f065356c597e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Speaker Johnson just revealed plans to tack the SAVE Act — one of the most extreme anti-voter bills in recent history — on to funding for the Department of Homeland Security. They’re going to try to pass this without needing to reach the 60-vote threshold in the Senate.
These guys think voters aren’t paying attention. [**Let’s show them they’re dead wrong — send an urgent message to Congress right now and tell them to stop the SAVE Act.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124671258/599339448/395572353?source=eng_aotl_tier1_email_SaveActRR_email_20260203-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActRR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=eng&utm_content=20260203-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActRR_&utm_campaign=SaveActRR&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjdlYWJhMmJhLTVkMDEtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=3l1dUAWVZob8s0lKE9U83MEfIbrOUd5eltfo3Hk8aOg=&emci=9af87dd8-5201-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=7eaba2ba-5d01-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=8431045)
If you don’t remember our fight to defeat the SAVE Act last year, this bill is designed to create barriers that would make it harder for millions of Americans to vote — all in the name of a voter fraud crisis that simply doesn’t exist.
Here’s who could be affected:
* Married women who have changed their last names and don’t have a birth certificate with their current legal name.
* Military voters who will no longer be able to use their military ID to register.
* Americans who don’t have a passport, who are more likely to come from lower-income families.
* Transgender Americans who have changed their legal names.
* Rural voters who often rely on online and mail-in voter registration.
* People who have lost documents to natural disasters, and so many more.

The House narrowly passed the SAVE Act last year but the Senate didn’t have the votes to take it up. With President Trump calling for the federal government to “take over” elections this week, it’s no wonder that anti-democracy lawmakers are trying again.
They know they need to stoop to sneaky maneuvers to pass this unpopular bill. As Senate Majority Leader John Thune said, “Any legislative vehicle that crosses the floor could be a candidate for an amendment vote.”

Peter ,
House Republicans just dropped a bill they’re calling the “Make Elections Great Again Act.” Don’t let the name fool you – it’s one of the most aggressive voter suppression schemes we’ve seen in years.
This bill would:
* Require strict photo ID to vote
* Force proof of citizenship to register – even for people already on the rolls
* Purge voter rolls every 30 days
* Ban universal vote-by-mail
* Green-light lawsuits against election officials doing their jobs
An estimated 21 million Americans don’t have proof of citizenship readily available. Millions more rely on mail voting because of work schedules, caregiving, disability, or distance. That’s not a bug of this bill – it’s the point.
Donald Trump has been blunt about why this is happening. He knows he’s unpopular. He knows midterms are coming. And he knows the only way Republicans hold power is by shrinking the electorate.
At GOTV PAC, we don’t just sound the alarm – we organize against it. We fund direct voter outreach, protect access at the ground level, and help campaigns reach voters Republicans are trying to erase from the system.
That work takes resources – and it takes them now, before suppression laws can do real damage.

| I’m shaken to my core by what we’re witnessing across our country right now.

I know this is personal for so many of you, and it should be. As a former DOJ attorney who spent more than two decades working on immigration issues — including enforcement — I believe deeply that in the United States, the Constitution and the rule of law must guide how federal agents operate.

But right now, agents are operating with too few checks on their authority and too little oversight. I’ve voted against funding bills that expand authority without accountability, because protecting communities and upholding justice is important.

**That’s why I’m committed to enforcing true accountability, restoring oversight of federal agencies, and making sure everyday Americans are protected.**

Thank you,

Hillary Scholten

name: info@luceroforcongress.com
subject: Rob Lucero - leading challenger to Gomez for Congress
body:
Thank you. Because of your support and contributions, the newly filed FEC reports for the end of 2025 show that Rob Lucero is now the leading challenger to incumbent Jimmy Gomez in California’s 34th Congressional District. Rob has pulled ahead of other candidates and established himself as the strongest alternative in the June open primary.

| | |
---
Hi Peter, Thank you. Because of your support and contributions, the newly filed FEC reports for the end of 2025 show that Rob Lucero is now the leading challenger to incumbent Jimmy Gomez in California’s 34th Congressional District. Rob has pulled ahead of other candidates and established himself as the strongest alternative in the June open primary. Rob is competing against candidates backed by well-funded national political organizations like the “Justice Democrats”. Despite that, this campaign, powered by grassroots supporters like you, has surged forward. This is the direct result of people deciding that Los Angeles and the nation deserve better representation and stepping up to make it happen. Jimmy Gomez has been in office since 2017. After years of Jimmy’s go-along, get-along politics in Washington, Los Angeles is still a mess: struggling with homelessness, public safety concerns, drug addiction, and a lack of serious leadership willing to address root causes instead of scoring partisan points. Endless finger-pointing and shouting about ICE and Trump have not fixed what families here are living with every day. Rob Lucero is offering something different. He is running on a positive platform of big ideas. How can America restore its manufacturing? How can we create tens of millions of new, well-paid jobs that can’t be taken by AI? What can we do about thousands of bridges that so badly need repair they’re on the verge of collapse? Lead pipe water systems that are delivering contaminated water? And he has specific answers to those questions that can be agreed upon by Democrats and Republicans. Rob Lucero is more focused on getting things done for the American people than Jimmy Gomez, who is probably secretly grateful for the excesses of ICE, so he doesn’t have to answer the question: what have you been doing these last eight years? Jimmy hopes he can ride the wave of party polarization - the cheap politics everyone is tired of. Rob understands that most people go to sleep worrying about their next paycheck, what their kids are being taught in school, and how they can afford gas and food. The latest fundraising results confirm what many voters are beginning to see: Rob is the candidate with the credibility, momentum, and a growing base of support to challenge the status quo and win. If you believe the second largest city in America deserves a real alternative, now is the moment to act. A contribution today helps us accelerate outreach, expand voter contact, and carry this momentum into the crucial months ahead of the June open primary. Together, we can turn this progress into a victory.

name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
subject: Continuing this important work
body:
| | Peter,

Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to make good on my promise to listen and bring all of our voices to the table, even when that means making tough decisions.

Let me be very clear: I am horrified by what has happened in Minnesota, and I am pushing for an independent investigation to bring transparency and accountability for the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti.

I am also calling on my fellow members to strategically use every tool at our disposal to secure meaningful structural reforms to ICE’s leadership and operations, rather than embracing the false narrative that shutdowns solve problems.

Keeping the government open while negotiations continue means that Congress can maintain its oversight authority, and avoid unnecessary strain on our communities and economy.

Rest assured that I will continue to work towards bipartisan solutions to protect public safety and our constitutional rights.

Your feedback is always important to me, so please feel free to share any thoughts or concerns by replying directly to this email.

Thanks for all you do.

Marie

P.S. Thanks to all who pitched in to help meet our January goal. We still have a lot of work to do as we look toward Election Day, and your support makes it all possible.

Trump’s order is the culmination of years of attacks on absentee ballots and vote-by-mail. In the months before the 2020 election, Trump repeatedly spread disinformation and conspiracy theories about the legitimacy of mail-in ballots as he campaigned for reelection. With MAGA angling for total control, Trump wants to end their use forever.
Fuel our work with $35 or more right now to help defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020326_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Democracy Docket: With New Order, Trump Tries to Kill Off Vote By Mail [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020326_3&amount=25]
We're going to keep hammering this home, Team, because the mainstream media continues to ignore this executive order and how it will change our elections forever.
President Donald Trump's massive anti-voting executive order has sent lawmakers, election officials, and voting rights advocates into a frenzy. One provision focuses on a goal that for years has been a borderline obsession for MAGA: Cracking down on voting by mail .
For background: After every election in which he's been a candidate or in power, Trump has raged over the use of mail-in ballots in general and ballot deadlines in particular . He's tried to claim fraud for every single ballot counted after Election Day.
So of course, this order directs Attorney General Pam Bondi to “ take all necessary action ” against any states that count absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day.
This order makes it clear that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
We've got to keep fighting and work to protect our elections and our fundamental right to vote. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020326_3&amount=35]

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . Elderly voters, the disabled, our military service members -- they all vote by mail.
Mail-in voting has happened dating back to the Civil War. It's always been safe and secure , mail-in voting fraud is supremely rare. States have spent millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing. It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
Our partners at VoteAmerica said it best: “ There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access, reject ballots without postmarks, or refuse to count ballots that arrive after Election Day. If the administration moves forward with these proposals, they will effectively disenfranchise older voters, rural voters, and military voters. ”
Opponents of voting rights have proven they'll go to any length necessary to stop people from voting and make sure that they stay in power. Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Listening to Texans is my favorite part of this campaign
body:
It takes a lot of resources to travel across the country’s second-largest state!
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
I had a _very_ busy January on the road, Peter!
I’m traveling across Texas because I believe the next Governor should earn every vote by showing up, listening, and fighting for people across our state.
**[If you can, will you chip in $5 right now to help keep me on the road and keep building this movement?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=1&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&amount=5&refcode=em20260203-522&t=20&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
Getting to hear directly from Texans and listening to their stories is one of the best parts of this campaign. **Here are a few highlights from the trail:**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=21&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
I supported union leader and veteran **Taylor Rehmet** in Fort Worth, where he just won his Texas Senate race and flipped a deep-red, gerrymandered district. **It was a powerful reminder that when you put workers first, fight for public schools, and stand up to corporate greed, Texans will stand with you.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=22&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
I joined thousands of San Antonians for the 2.75-mile MLK March — **the largest MLK march in the nation.** It’s an incredible tradition, and it reminded me how much power there is when communities come together.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=23&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
I spent time in **Houston** talking with community members about the real harm Greg Abbott’s leadership has done — and what it will mean for our communities if he’s reelected. **Houstonians are paying attention,** and they’re ready for something better.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=24&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
I attended a lotería in **Hidalgo** and shared why I’m running. I was born and raised in the Valley, so being back home is always a great time to connect with my community. It’s also a reminder that Texas doesn’t just deserve better leadership — **we deserve leadership that understands our communities firsthand and isn’t out of touch.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=25&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
I visited **Books are GEMS in El Paso,** an incredible nonprofit making sure families and public schools have access to books at a time when so many are being priced out. Organizations like this are doing the work to lift communities up, and our state government should be doing the same.
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&amount=5&refcode=em20260203-522&t=26&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
What I’m certain of after these days on the trail is that Texans are done with Abbott’s corruption, and they’re done with leaders who work for the wealthy and well-connected instead of everyone else.
These are just a few of the stops from a packed January. And everywhere I go, I hear the same thing. This isn’t about blue or red. It’s about whether our leaders will actually work for Texans.
With the primary election less than a month away, we need to prove our people-powered movement can compete with Greg Abbott’s massive war chest. **[If you’re able, please rush $5 today to help keep me traveling, organizing, and talking to Texans across the state.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&refcode=em20260203-522&amount=5&t=27&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260203_1_trail.YRPvpO&amount=5&refcode=em20260203-522&t=28&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)
Thank you for your support, and I hope to see you on the road soon!
— Gina

[ Donate » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20260203-1&t=29&refcode2=522_299639_LwRmWP&akid=522%2E299639%2ELwRmWP)

---
| | Friends,
Michigan is winnable in 2026, but only if Republicans nominate candidates who can win statewide and govern competently once elected.
In a competitive state like Michigan, down-ballot races such as Attorney General and Secretary of State can make or break the entire ticket. In elections like this, experience, electability, and institutional knowledge of the Democratic opposition matter. Strong candidates lift the ticket. Weak ones can drag it down, as outlined in a recent analysis on electability: [The RIGHT Side News](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001CmfDElULkSo5o_BD-e4QtVX309fSicnlAh2VYtzK_tvw4STIxkE5xuZSKnBRcs1YTA3m9ZS-OWL9hZZKJr5eajAJx_kzpDkbK8wevP-aVLp5h05xxwkQLqInkeLqRyGn1wo7w0bpU1m_BFzf5wJ3kgIlQrLvKe97jAG5BehiD_2BRcxAMnok7oCfJTqIkfuukjP1-7kTP0-tNVPb35_ldO0yFj7O40SBvu0OgX6-Wd7uPd-nIys44iNIhiEP0_jmjMSHVbZRGLA=&c=0B1gqhnTFKmZvyUhlTuq9pppEMhnBN2pWNYv12rV_w2rS373n-qOYg==&ch=di8WzYVgbCfoM4YSvIiOUIpZdtPB_uf5VyroS1rwO2VxXMG4lcIWqg==)
I am running for Attorney General because I bring the professionally relevant experience, judgment, and proven leadership required for the job. The Attorney General's office is not a training ground. It is a constitutional office with broad authority that demands a deep understanding of law enforcement, government, and the limits of power.
That experience matters now more than ever because the likely Democratic nominee, Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald, is not a symbolic candidate. She has aligned herself with the activist approach of Dana Nessel, Gretchen Whitmer, and Jocelyn Benson. Her public praise for Nessel's lawsuits against President Trump makes clear that the same political activism would continue, this time with greater reach and sophistication.
That is what makes this race dangerous. A progressive Democrat with prosecutorial credentials and an activist mindset can do real damage from the Attorney General's office.
Michigan cannot afford Dana Nessel 2.0.
Republicans must nominate a candidate who can credibly contrast that record with respect for the rule of law, public safety, and constitutional limits. I bring experience directly aligned with the duties of the Attorney General, a record of enforcing the law without politicizing it, and the credibility to win independents and moderate Democrats who decide statewide elections.
I ask delegates to look beyond campaign branding and slogans. This race is about whether we nominate a prepared, proven candidate who strengthens the ticket, or someone whose lack of readiness or personal vulnerabilities become a liability Democrats will exploit.
Voters want competence. They want experience. And they want an Attorney General who will protect their rights, improve public safety, and keep law enforcement out of partisan politics.
I entered this race to win and to restore the Michigan Attorney General's office to its proper role. With your support, we can lift the ticket, defeat the Democrats in November, and put Michigan back on the right track.
Join me. Together, we can win.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

clean_body: Strong Leadership Lifts the Ticket | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, Michigan is winnable in 2026, but only if Republicans nominate candidates who can win statewide and govern competently once elected. In a competitive state like Michigan, down-ballot races such as Attorney General and Secretary of State can make or break the entire ticket. In elections like this, experience, electability, and institutional knowledge of the Democratic opposition matter. Strong candidates lift the ticket. Weak ones can drag it down, as outlined in a recent analysis on electability: == I am running for Attorney General because I bring the professionally relevant experience, judgment, and proven leadership required for the job. The Attorney General's office is not a training ground. It is a constitutional office with broad authority that demands a deep understanding of law enforcement, government, and the limits of power. That experience matters now more than ever because the likely Democratic nominee, Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald, is not a symbolic candidate. She has aligned herself with the activist approach of Dana Nessel, Gretchen Whitmer, and Jocelyn Benson. Her public praise for Nessel's lawsuits against President Trump makes clear that the same political activism would continue, this time with greater reach and sophistication. That is what makes this race dangerous. A progressive Democrat with prosecutorial credentials and an activist mindset can do real damage from the Attorney General's office. Michigan cannot afford Dana Nessel 2.0. Republicans must nominate a candidate who can credibly contrast that record with respect for the rule of law, public safety, and constitutional limits. I bring experience directly aligned with the duties of the Attorney General, a record of enforcing the law without politicizing it, and the credibility to win independents and moderate Democrats who decide statewide elections. I ask delegates to look beyond campaign branding and slogans. This race is about whether we nominate a prepared, proven candidate who strengthens the ticket, or someone whose lack of readiness or personal vulnerabilities become a liability Democrats will exploit. Voters want competence. They want experience. And they want an Attorney General who will protect their rights, improve public safety, and keep law enforcement out of partisan politics. I entered this race to win and to restore the Michigan Attorney General's office to its proper role. With your support, we can lift the ticket, defeat the Democrats in November, and put Michigan back on the right track. Join me. Together, we can win. Defend Our Courts has been sounding the alarm about Trump's plot to rig elections since our founding in Spring 2025.
In our first major race, the '25 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election, we laid out the stakes for Democrats: Trump is attempting to take control of PA state Supreme Court so that he will have control over the court with final say on election related matters in the most important swing state in America.
In short, we've been warning that Trump is trying to control how states run their elections by planting his loyalist judges on State Supreme Courts.
Our critics called us "alarmist." MAGA called us crazy.
But what Donald Trump announced proves without a doubt that the plot we have been warning about is very, very real:

Trump is now openly declaring his war on free and fair elections.
In the Constitution, it clearly outlines that state governments, not the federal government, have responsibility for how elections are administered. It's literally in the first Article of the Constitution.
And that means there's good news and bad news:
The good news: Trump's call to nationalize elections is so unconstitutional that even the MAGA controlled Supreme Court is unlikely to allow it.
The bad news: Now that Trump has publicly stated his end goal, MAGA's going to go nuclear to try and take control of state Supreme Courts across the country.
Defend Our Court's mission has never been more essential to preserving Democracy than it is now.
In 2026, there are state Supreme Court elections in several key swing states; Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
Last year, Defend Our Courts helped spearhead the defense of PA's state Supreme Court. And Democrats there didn't just win, they won massive 30+ point landslides. | Friend,
Defend Our Courts has been sounding the alarm about Trump's plot to rig elections since our founding in Spring 2025.
In our first major race, the '25 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election, we laid out the stakes for Democrats: Trump is attempting to take control of PA state Supreme Court so that he will have control over the court with final say on election related matters in the most important swing state in America.
In short, we've been warning that Trump is trying to control how states run their elections by planting his loyalist judges on State Supreme Courts.
Our critics called us "alarmist." MAGA called us crazy. But what Donald Trump announced proves without a doubt that the plot we have been warning about is very, very real:

---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001jkJpAtYZLuO-Y4peb7EDnwF6H1WfnJA6nA3G06tClN4TxeBYybs8NhKJ9e3qbaUmp07Qhw1y99aI9lJwt6oYkKipkRnOTEcHhRQWMz4iMatpB3wcH-4AXspYKdd-Ua794c-26Mi2Yn0zp5CBeTVCQwyTCpVuoGI8TGjK-_MhlTJqY6CUrZhG8RG8LT1UZ7IbDMsbz3KNx0-8DHdoYiSXonIeuS9SlbHsWHZxgkvf6iez9H9b5GXpy_IMTKaaEEkyNa5nb-KdSaA=&c=HoB9jWIqRcdmQJe-M3bLMGP79iKWoZZ3pOX6yLo0LDE8SlSyTYr62Q==&ch=JHZsyGURa8iLg2A4kEnQclfEH4uxXhWhsA5IZwzW4Kxnem4QT7pSsA==)
---
Trump is now openly declaring his war on free and fair elections.
In the Constitution, it clearly outlines that state governments, not the federal government, have responsibility for how elections are administered. It's literally in the first Article of the Constitution.
And that means there's good news and bad news:
The good news: Trump's call to nationalize elections is so unconstitutional that even the MAGA controlled Supreme Court is unlikely to allow it.
The bad news: Now that Trump has publicly stated his end goal, MAGA's going to go nuclear to try and take control of state Supreme Courts across the country.
Defend Our Court's mission has never been more essential to preserving Democracy than it is now.
In 2026, there are state Supreme Court elections in several key swing states; Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
Last year, Defend Our Courts helped spearhead the defense of PA's state Supreme Court. And Democrats there didn't just win, they won massive 30+ point landslides. ## Central Texas Students Protest ICE in Walkout
Attorney General Ken Paxton has requested records from Austin ISD related to anti-ICE protests at 14 campuses last week. On Monday, students in several other Central Texas school districts [walked out of class](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMhp8GuowSE2CuSHEN3V57JfIkZrAuJAibnZ23P7GvsJWLT_r0-f_7MX8gZy7PP7hR0K-lzoVekkmVjlnpC4tw0ZVqfm87R5F4PjDNYGEwFoz1c0LO79m3KTxs-uVaCm4cLdiht327BnDUwQj9QDjcl9776-DgsMMlorUth0tmwXoH1vnu5vyd3N0PQJi66LHxlhJrPW660pUkS37XTzpusW5tDqvqLk33u4GpgSk-BE9RLhdtYLreaWDKNWK-MBU9MJtvjxE9ExUVE2tRLieZF-Z_XJ6mnmrqYmJGEaPV7EdVEjUcydSdDlSuRdojpP3FObMMY-Ptc0PO31n6szE_A_wPAAD___OYjRc) to protest ICE operations. Paxton is asking for information about excused absence policies, security protocols, and internal communications about the protests. "_Parents expect our public schools to educate and keep their kids safe during the school day, not encourage them to attend a protest field trip designed to villainize brave law enforcement officials protecting our country_ ," [he said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdI7WizGhoLiG7r_2SrSxl8SKYyO8geTtT9wrXDsjjb75_vzMPxRTzPff9OJRPkuZMx81sQhvs_CHco1ZHlzS97VGX6t_3yjMCOg0oAY7B4rpO9smjDcIg2l4NH0PCK6DrnmMprPGBs-dsb5z3WL7Djwszg1E0C_QxPEcAwRrEIxtL8Ze2VytQ6bQekvKAocoZbvIg0-kuqRv2Xm7-PJq0vgQWatqfymcFE7HcVye-5vPUuFEm0SfWOF0_lI4peIpKZzWrQhXOaMnZ73SR0rW9K4Ss4416IPSs7yl6ph3rhLvJLFkhRO6QQ-eYDHtoLnloG3gQV_b4LQxzrR4a3tr-2Ybw3rElGJ1vbJwf1FM_5jl_0zvI_4NAAD__2WdkXw). Several hundred students at five Hays CISD high schools participated in the walkout, along with students at five Pflugerville ISD campuses, three Manor ISD campuses, and Lockhart High School. "_It just popped up on Instagram . . . so we decided to hop on too_ ," [said Alex Valencia](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOgzAQBNCvgQ603jiYFC6uocu1V6INXoIlgxG7CeHvT9wvXD96mpmfe3-nmOLy_KaZvX7G3C-8S2JV3nrlDy0SF504p2Ne4yAyvB4UegRsKsAKbB8opqO3ZfAPCDdTsjfOAUJzhWs5-bZ5GOTrzZBDbAPB2FAYrHNgCMLNldGfGCBYg2DspTa2ZdPaBpnCZbBUWOAQNW-1TnxWkjEd-c1bPeS5TH5SXaW4fBXYFdjt-16P-ePoJRqXM1Jgd24qsJvokGqIEirRV-BFq3XLyqJSbj6se0wpSuMKC8-ZYvrz9X-vvD3-BgAA__91IXgb), a senior at Lehman High School in Kyle.
## SpaceX Acquiring xAI
SpaceX is [acquiring](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOrDAQRE8DmZExBkPg4Cdk89MNUY_dHloymKXNwNx-xV5h81LVq_f1mB5AkdbXf1jQ5iukacWTI-aM-5TxgpVpzTOm-Fk2cszueIKflFSdkEpIPXmg-Jl06e1T-qEu0dbGSCW7VrblbH2jzWBah0OvTa9VGIzSYQAT0AXfypLsXSaV1LWStW6qWvdY97pTCL5xGgot0VNOe5VnvJE4xE964165tJTRzjlvXDT_CjUWajzPswrpeh5MKzLfmUKNIV3iPibYEa4OCzXyBg4vAe77oB1ZXEBiR5d2LxhzpvUlPEIUb4gHenEPijqXu_XbSTESd6bQ8rUAxV-Q_Dd9b6t-AgAA__9U_oeA) xAI—the AI startup known for its chatbot Grok and social media platform X—according to a Monday announcement from Elon Musk, who founded and leads both companies. SpaceX is headquartered in Starbase, while X is based in Bastrop. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Donald Trump just won big... Friend,

In less than two weeks, millions of people will gather to watch the biggest football game of the year. **Bright lights.**
**Packed hotels.** **Most people don't know this...** Wherever crowds gather, traffickers follow. Major sporting weekends bring increased travel, full hotels, busy airports, and distracted attention. **Behind the excitement ...**
**Children will go missing.** This is the perfect environment for exploitation. Law enforcement and child protection organizations know this pattern well. **Trafficking spikes around large events because vulnerability increases. **While millions are preparing for entertainment, vulnerable children are facing danger. They're not thinking about scores or highlights, but hoping to be safe - waiting for help before harm happens. This is why this moment matters. Here is a truth that should stop us cold: **9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked right here in the United States.** That's why I'm reaching out to you today. The**Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to interrupt these moments of danger with protection, prevention, and action. We are not here for awareness alone.Awareness without action does not save a child. We are here to stop trafficking before it starts, support intervention efforts, and protect children when the risk is highest. **But this mission is not an idea. ****It is personal. **
**It is lived. **
**It is carried by those who know danger firsthand.**

My name is Theresa Flores. I'm a survivor of child trafficking. And today, I work to help protect children **before they disappear.** **I was fifteen years old. **
**An honor student. **
**A daughter. ** A girl who trusted the wrong "friend." **I was trafficked for two years.**

Most people imagine trafficking happens far away...in dark alleys...in other countries.

To "other people." **But that's not how it usually happens.** Right now, as set up for the big game is underway, **120 trained partner volunteers are already on the ground in the Bay Area**. Men and women working _this week_ --
Training hotel staff to recognize danger. Walking hotel halls, parking garages and public spaces. **Watching.**
**Reporting.**
**Protecting.** **Standing where traffickers don't expect resistance.** Children cannot choose safety on their own. They depend on adults to act when danger is highest. Freedom is not a word painted in an end zone. It's safety, dignity and the chance to grow up without fear. Your donation right now helps fund prevention programs, strengthen intervention efforts, and protect innocent lives from trafficking and abuse.It turns high-risk moments into moments of defense and hope.

Behind the excitement ... Children will go missing. This is the perfect environment for exploitation. Law enforcement and child protection organizations know this pattern well. They're not thinking about scores or highlights, but hoping to be safe - waiting for help before harm happens. This is why this moment matters. I was fifteen years old. An honor student. A daughter. A girl who trusted the wrong "friend." I was trafficked for two years. Most people imagine trafficking happens far away...in dark alleys...in other countries. To "other people." But that's not how it usually happens. Right now, as set up for the big game is underway, 120 trained partner volunteers are already on the ground in the Bay Area. Men and women working this week -- Training hotel staff to recognize danger. Walking hotel halls, parking garages and public spaces. Watching. Reporting. Protecting. Standing where traffickers don't expect resistance. Children cannot choose safety on their own. They depend on adults to act when danger is highest. Freedom is not a word painted in an end zone. It's safety, dignity and the chance to grow up without fear. Your donation right now helps fund prevention programs, strengthen intervention efforts, and protect innocent lives from trafficking and abuse.It turns high-risk moments into moments of defense and hope. The game will last a few hours. Your impact lasts a lifetime. # **Minnesota church congregants face ongoing harassment after anti-ICE protest disruption**
Caleb Phillips, a 21-year-old regular attendee of Cities Church in St. Paul, Minnesota, said **[leftist agitators have continued to harass and heckle congregants](https://substack.com/redirect/2c327ec6-71b6-4b32-9200-531781af8aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for two consecutive Sundays following their January 18 disruption of a service, when dozens of anti-ICE protesters stormed the sanctuary screaming chants and causing children to cry.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c327ec6-71b6-4b32-9200-531781af8aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The protesters targeted the church because one of its pastors is associated with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, accusing congregants of "harboring" him and saying they "should be ashamed as a church" and are "not real Christians." Phillips described the invasion as a "traumatic scenario" but said services have been "packed" in response.
* **What they 're saying:** Phillips and his Asian girlfriend attempted to pray with some protesters after a service, but a protester with a megaphone then berated his girlfriend with racial attacks, saying "You're Asian, why are you hanging out with Nazis" and "they're going to come for her next." Phillips called it a "spiritual battle" and said congregants will continue to "love those who hate us and pray for those who persecute us."
* **The response:** Despite feeling anger at the hatred directed at them, Phillips said the church will not "shun our brother in Christ because his line of work isn't popular right now," and congregants responded to the initial invasion by singing, praying, and reading scripture while young church members faced down the agitators.

* * *
# **Failed Trump assassin to be sentenced**
Ryan Routh, 59, **[will be sentenced Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/323c48eb-4d61-4623-8d62-ef3b67a90025?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon for attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump at his West Palm Beach golf course in September 2024. The Justice Department is requesting a life sentence, stating "Routh's crimes undeniably warrant a life sentence--he took steps over the course of months to assassinate a major Presidential candidate."
* **What happened:** Secret Service Agent Robert Fercano spotted Routh embedded in a hedge near the sixth hole with a rifle on September 15, 2024, and opened fire, prompting Routh to flee. He left behind an SKS-style rifle with scope, extra ammunition, steel armor plates, and a camera. Cell phone records showed his phones pinged near the golf course and Mar-a-Lago multiple times from August 18 to September 15.
* **The evidence:** Investigators found a list of Trump's scheduled appearances, a notebook with ramblings about fighting for Ukraine, and a letter Routh wrote offering "$150,000 to whomever can complete the job" of assassinating Trump. Routh was also convicted of possessing a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence, assaulting a federal officer, and other weapons charges. When the verdict was delivered in September 2025, Routh attempted to stab himself in the neck with a pen.

# _**Come on dude!**_**Mamdani fails to handle massive snow storm, gets a custom winter jacket instead**
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faced criticism for **[apparently prioritizing his appearance over the city's response](https://substack.com/redirect/29375b18-50a4-4f5a-b0a0-b51329163f32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to Winter Storm Fern, which killed 16 people and left streets buried in snow and trash. The New York Times reported Monday that while coordinating the citywide response, the mayor "wanted to find a new coat" that was "unassuming and modest, but still able to distinguish him."

But outrage grew as the death toll rose and trash piled up on snow-covered streets, with critics saying "if he used a fraction of the energy spent on his propaganda videos and prop jackets towards running the city, we wouldn't have people literally dying."

"He literally has his head in the clouds while people are literally dying on the streets," one political strategist said.

# **Tyler Robinson defense claims Utah prosecutor sought death penalty to please Trump in Charlie Kirk assassination case**
Alleged Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson's defense team argued during a Tuesday pre-trial hearing that Utah County Attorney Jeffrey S. Gray only moved to seek the death penalty because **[President Trump had publicly declared his wish to see Kirk's killer executed,](https://substack.com/redirect/d99b8f82-a90d-4b0b-8e34-c0abaf00d2b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** questioning whether Gray was motivated by "strong emotional reactions" rather than legal considerations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d99b8f82-a90d-4b0b-8e34-c0abaf00d2b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Defense attorney Richard Novak raised potential conflicts of interest including Gray's 2022 campaign promise to seek the death penalty in "appropriate" cases, the fact that an adult child of a prosecutor in Gray's office witnessed the shooting, and Trump's social media post stating "I hope he gets the death penalty." The defense sought to have Gray's office removed from the case.

* **What Gray said:** The prosecutor denied that Trump's statements, his campaign promises, or the prosecutor's child being present influenced his decision-making. Gray testified he announced the death penalty decision early to "limit speculation from social media and the press" and lessen anxiety for victims, particularly Kirk's widow Erika Kirk, adding that both he and Governor Spencer Cox determined capital punishment was appropriate in this case.

As always, to stay up to date on late-breaking stories and analysis, [subscribe to our daily email list](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=3d1b8b5c6e&e=b7b3eddce2) and get the best of _Broad + Liberty_ delivered straight to your inbox.

# **[1\. Minneapolis or Nashville — which path will Philly choose?](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=77234155cc&e=b7b3eddce2)**
_By Guy Ciarrocchi_ Organized chaos in Minneapolis. It’s been in the spotlight — understandably. ICE raids. Protests. Confrontation. Deaths. Over 3,000 arrests and counting of known illegal immigrant murderers, rapists, kidnappers and child traffickers. The last part may be news to many because so much noise — mostly contrived — has been made about ICE that much of legacy news has “overlooked” what ICE has thankfully accomplished. We should never forget that if the protestors had their way — and those who fund and orchestrate their efforts — every single one of those 3,000-plus thugs would still be walking the streets. Where we live, work and our children play. **Why It Matters.** Compare this with Nashville, Tennessee. No national news stories about that Democrat-run city. No protests. No confrontations. No inquiries to ICE agents. And, thankfully, no deaths to civilians or agents. Why? Because the mayor and his team respect the rule of law, public safety — and, accept the results of the 2024 election. Just as local law enforcement works with the FBI, DEA, the Coast Guard, state police and National Guard, Tennessee law enforcement is cooperating with ICE and CBP. This protects everyone’s rights, minimizes confrontation, and focuses on everyone’s safety. As the focus on ICE intensifies, Parker, Shapiro and other politicians will have to chart their course. Nashville or Minneapolis? Virtue-signaling and grandstanding or common-sense governing? [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=3def3d3e12&e=b7b3eddce2)

|
---
|
# **[2\. Krasner’s latest ploy — the ‘FAFO Coalition’](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=9728b8ad5e&e=b7b3eddce2)**
_By Ben Mannes_ Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner escalated his public rhetoric over federal immigration authorities by unveiling a national coalition of like‐minded local prosecutors sharing the same donors, of whom he said are ready to charge federal officers they believe break state criminal laws while enforcing immigration policy. The move renewed questions about constitutional limits on local authority over federal agents and about the funding networks backing Krasner and his new political allies. At a press conference in Center City, Krasner announced what he called the “FAFO collision,” a political and legal partnership with nine other elected prosecutors from jurisdictions that have clashed with federal immigration enforcement. The group publicly brands itself as “Fight Against Federal Overreach,” or FAFO, a name that also echoes a profane online slogan about the consequences of bad behavior that Krasner has used to “appear tough” in prior public remarks about law enforcement accountability. **Why It Matters.** Krasner’s announcement comes amid a series of Philadelphia events in which he has[ _vulgarly “warned”_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=2bdb5a7f15&e=b7b3eddce2) ICE and other federal agents they could be arrested if they commit what he deems crimes in the city, including a recent[ _news conference_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=b61955020f&e=b7b3eddce2) condemning a fatal ICE shooting in Minneapolis. In that earlier appearance, he told agents who “come to Philly to commit crimes” to “get the F out of here” and vowed to charge any officer involved in a similar killing locally. That tension — between local outrage over high‐profile enforcement incidents and the legal shield around federal authority — is at the center of Krasner’s campaign. Ironically, Article VI supremacy is the clause that enabled federal enforcement to the laws that ended a ban on gay marriage, slavery, and segregation. # 4\. What we're reading

In _The Federalist_ this week, [_Rachel Bovard asks_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=0e33f5e312&e=b7b3eddce2) , “What if I told you Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., has the power and the votes — right now — to save Republicans’ congressional majorities, President Trump’s second-term agenda, and maybe the republic itself, all while poleaxing Democrats on the short side of an 84-15 issue?” The issue to which she refers is voter identification — specifically the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, which would require all Americans to prove their citizenship to be eligible to vote. It’s a simple idea — being a citizen is _already_ a requirement for voting. So why do Senate Dems threaten to filibuster the bill? And why don’t Republicans call their bluff? This is an issue the vast majority of Americans agree about – the senator should debate it openly and let the people see where they stand.

Hey y’all, I’m Marina, and I’m part of the Hines Leadership Fellows, a group of interns for Christina Hines.
I am sure you’ve seen the headlines. If you’re like me, you’re feeling overwhelmed, discouraged, and, honestly, scared about where American politics is headed.
I’m worried about getting a good-paying job after I graduate, my generation’s trust in our government is at an all-time low, and our communities are paying the price for the people in Washington that aren’t paying attention to working families and young people.
As a first-generation college student who grew up during the pandemic, I’m tired of feeling afraid—and even more tired of leaders who do nothing while things get worse.
That’s why I’m working for Christina. Because I know that if we come together, we can flip the House blue and elect someone who will actually fight for us.
If you can, please consider donating $25 today. It helps cover things like gas, so we can organize events, recruit volunteers, and keep showing up for Christina and Michigan. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q1?refcode=x_260204_MarinasPOV_act&amount=25]

When I saw this opportunity with Christina’s campaign, I looked her up. I saw she’s a former prosecutor who spent her career taking on sex crimes and human trafficking cases. Her whole job was standing up for people who don’t always have a voice and holding abusers accountable.
I saw what she stood for, and I knew I wanted to stand for it, too.
Now, I’m working with folks like you to get the word out about our grassroots campaign to make real, lasting change for Michigan.
The 2026 election is coming up fast, and people-powered campaigns like ours don’t have corporate money to fall back on. What we do have is people like you and me—students, workers, families—pitching in when it matters most.
Please donate $25 today to help keep our campaign moving forward. Your contribution helps make sure our voices are finally represented in Congress. In 2007, former U.S. Representative William J. Jefferson, a Democrat from Louisiana, became a symbol of [political scandal](https://substack.com/redirect/4ac88b31-cd47-4969-b036-a0dee5d33e39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when the FBI discovered $90,000 in marked cash hidden in his freezer during a bribery investigation.

This cash was part of a sting operation where Jefferson allegedly accepted bribes to influence business deals in Africa.

He was indicted on 16 counts, including bribery, racketeering, and money laundering, and convicted on 11 of them in 2009.

Jefferson received a 13-year prison sentence, though a 2016 Supreme Court ruling on corruption definitions led to the dismissal of several charges, resulting in his release in 2017 after serving about five years.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.n9HDMnySHPxYxCCvH_vAA4apsmWxUwaV1_fAztDoziE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186859397)
By no means was his scrutiny the first for a politician, for example Hazel O'Leary's tenure as Energy Secretary mortified her boss by jetting away on lavish trips. Her most embarrassing misstep was the Justice Department examining Democratic moneyman [Johnny Chung's allegations that O'Leary](https://substack.com/redirect/960d8cc7-ce0f-4e79-8ed3-61b00cc1b5c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) met with Chinese officials in return for his $25,000 "donation" to a charity she supported called Africare.

But Jefferson's case drew national attention and raised questions about accountability in public office, particularly among elected officials from underrepresented groups.

Since Jefferson's scandal, there have been several high-profile cases involving Democratic politicians accused or convicted of misconduct while in office.
Public perceptions of corruption often align with partisan biases, with polls showing Americans viewing the opposing party as more corrupt--nearly 80% of both Democrats and Republicans believe corruption is a serious issue among presidents from the other side.
"You're not to be so blind with patriotism that you can't face reality. Wrong is wrong, no matter who does it or says it." Malcolm X
With that in mind, focusing on documented cases involving Democrats since 2007, drawing from verifiable convictions, indictments, and scandals, while noting that allegations do not always lead to guilt, it's not a good look for civic leaders.

Beyond Jefferson, several Democratic members of Congress have faced criminal convictions. Chaka Fattah, a long-serving representative from Pennsylvania, was convicted in 2016 on 23 counts of racketeering, fraud, and money laundering.

The charges stemmed from schemes to misuse campaign funds, nonprofit grants, and federal money for personal gain, including repaying illegal loans. Fattah, who had been in office since 1995, was sentenced to 10 years in prison and resigned amid the scandal.

Jesse Jackson Jr., son of civil rights leader Jesse Jackson and an Illinois congressman, pleaded guilty in 2013 to wire fraud and conspiracy for misusing over $750,000 in campaign funds on personal luxuries like fur capes and Michael Jackson memorabilia.

He served about two years in prison. His wife, Sandi Jackson, a Chicago alderman, was also convicted in the same scheme.

Corrine Brown, a Florida representative, was convicted in 2017 on 18 counts of fraud and tax evasion related to a sham charity that funneled donations for personal use.
She served nearly three years before her conviction was overturned on appeal in 2021 due to a juror issue, though she later pleaded guilty to tax fraud in a plea deal.
These cases highlight patterns of financial misconduct, while broader databases of legislator misconduct, tracking 504 instances since 1789, include ethics violations alongside crimes.
"[Politics is the art of making your selfish desires seem like the national interest.](https://substack.com/redirect/3bf6bc31-997a-436c-afe6-c66a11739f7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"
-- [Thomas Sowell](https://substack.com/redirect/0f22df55-e99b-43eb-9b9c-a8139056b3db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Big City Mayors: A Pattern of Scandals

Democratic mayors in major cities have been involved in several corruption cases since 2007, often involving misuse of public funds or bribery. Ray Nagin, former New Orleans mayor, [was convicted in 2014](https://substack.com/redirect/af755dac-fd4b-462f-ad96-50b1142d2837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on 20 counts of bribery and fraud for accepting kickbacks from contractors during Hurricane Katrina recovery.
He served nine years in prison.

Kwame Kilpatrick, Detroit's mayor, [resigned in 2008](https://substack.com/redirect/af0f3069-e4f2-4fbc-9d89-4f00dd47232e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) amid a perjury scandal but was convicted in 2013 on 24 federal counts of racketeering and extortion in a broader corruption probe.

Known as the "Hip-Hop Mayor," he spent over seven years incarcerated.

In Baltimore, [Sheila Dixon was convicted in 2009](https://substack.com/redirect/31e54281-79e5-42e4-8647-c2dc1e0dec77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of embezzling gift cards meant for needy families, leading to her resignation.

Her successor, Catherine Pugh, [pleaded guilty in 2019 to conspiracy](https://substack.com/redirect/774aba9c-98c9-481a-afdd-7aceec160d8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and tax evasion for fraudulent book sales tied to city contracts, serving three years.
Washington, D.C. Mayor Marion Barry was arrested in an FBI sting operation at the Vista Hotel, where he was videotaped smoking crack cocaine with a former model. A federal grand jury later indicted him on three felony counts of perjury (for lying to investigators) and five misdemeanor counts of cocaine possession stemming from multiple incidents.

Barry was sentenced to six months in federal prison. Despite the scandal, he later staged a political comeback, serving a fourth term as mayor from 1995 to 1999 and earning the nickname "Mayor for Life."

"There is hardly an office from United States Senator down to Alderman in any part of the country to which the business man has not been elected; yet politics remains corrupt, government pretty bad, and the selfish citizen has to hold himself in readiness like the old volunteer firemen to rush forth at any hour, in any weather, to prevent the fire; and he goes out sometimes and he puts out the fire (after the damage is done) and he goes back to the shop sighing for the business man in politics. The business man has failed in politics as he has in citizenship. Why?" [David Tucker](https://substack.com/redirect/486e4a81-7a96-4058-9eda-4dbf20fdb1df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
More recently, Chokwe Antar Lumumba, mayor of Jackson, Mississippi, was indicted in 2024 on federal bribery charges alongside the local DA for allegedly accepting bribes from developers.

Critics argue these cases reflect systemic issues in underfunded cities, but some see a pattern of Democrat leaders.

Police Chief incidents include Oakland's police department facing multiple scandals under various chiefs, including resignations amid sexual misconduct probes in the 2010s.

In Memphis, the department was investigated for civil rights violations in 2024 under Chief Cerelyn "CJ" Davis. The probe focused on excessive force patterns.
Carmen Best, Seattle's police chief, left her post, in the midst of protests against police brutality in her city.

Best announced her resignation after the city council approved a proposal to slash the police department budget by $4 million and cut as many as 100 officers from the force.

DC's Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) Chief Pamela Smith announced her resignation just days before federal lawmakers criticized her leadership. A report from the House Oversight Committee accuses her of coercing officers to manipulate crime data.

District Attorneys: Fani Willis, Letitia James, and Others

Fulton County DA Fani Willis, a Democrat, has been embroiled in controversy over her handling of the Georgia election interference case against Donald Trump. In 2024, she was disqualified from the case due to an alleged improper romantic relationship with special prosecutor Nathan Wade, which raised conflict-of-interest concerns.
She was also fined $54,000 in 2025 for violating Georgia's open records act by withholding documents.

New York AG Letitia James, also a Democrat, faced federal indictment in October 2025 for bank fraud and false statements related to misrepresenting a Virginia property purchase to secure a better loan.

James denies wrongdoing, calling it politically motivated.

Other DAs include Marilyn Mosby (Baltimore), convicted in 2024 of mortgage fraud for lying on loan applications, serving home detention after a pardon request.
Jody Owens (Jackson, MS) was [indicted in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/1ce18c10-0535-4dc0-9b52-9d25ffa1b983?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) alongside Mayor Lumumba.

Broader Context and Non-Partisan Perspective

In late 2017, amid the #MeToo movement, that the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights (formerly Office of Compliance) had paid out over $17 million in taxpayer funds since 1997 to settle hundreds of workplace disputes across the legislative branch, including some involving sexual harassment claims against members of Congress or their staff.

Known public cases involved members like Blake Farenthold (R-Tex., $84,000 taxpayer-funded settlement) and John Conyers (D-Mich., $27,000 from office funds),

In total, corruption erodes trust, with 70% of Americans believing ordinary people have too little influence compared to moneyed interests according to Pew research.

Addressing it requires systemic reforms like transparency and campaign finance limits, applicable to all parties. The cases since Jefferson underscore the need for vigilance, but corruption is a human failing, not a partisan or racial one. However, when a representative of a minority constituency goes down for corruption it hurts the whole community's character that MLK had such high aspirations for.

From documented federal congressional cases since 2007 suggest around 15-20 indictments total including Republicans (examples include): Chris Collins (R), Duncan Hunter (R), Jeff Fortenberry (R), Michael Grimm (R), Rick Renzi (R), George Santos (R, Brazilian-American but typically classified as white/Latino), Henry Cuellar (D, Latino), and others like Bob Menendez (D, Cuban-American).

[The Teapot Dome Scandal](https://substack.com/redirect/1cfb7529-7ee6-4c18-abf2-6b0d74412b08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was a huge government bribery and corruption case in the 1920s where the Secretary of the Interior, [Albert B. Fall](https://substack.com/redirect/aeaff254-ce78-48af-8dba-6fc990a5c24f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), secretly leased Navy oil reserves (like the Teapot Dome field in Wyoming) to private oil companies for large bribes, making him the first cabinet member jailed for crimes while in office and exposing corruption in President Harding's administration. Overall, there were a total of nine federal court trials and several appeals, leading to a number of indictments over a six-year period.

The **[Abscam](https://substack.com/redirect/13a33b83-0f6e-48cd-9959-1b724a51afda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ operation](https://substack.com/redirect/13a33b83-0f6e-48cd-9959-1b724a51afda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), initiated by the FBI in 1978, was the widest dragnet ever cast to prove wrongdoing on the part of public officials. The sting proved effective including a senator (Harrison Williams) and six congressmen (Frank Thompson, John Murphy, Michael Myers, Richard Kelly, Raymond Lederer, and John Jenrette).
At the state/local level (e.g., governors, legislators), indictments are more numerous. Known cases since 2007 (e.g., Rod Blagojevich, Andrew Gillum (acquitted). U.S. Congressman Dan Rostenkowski was indicted in **1994** on 17 felony counts for corruption, including mail/wire fraud, embezzlement, and obstruction, stemming from the House Post Office scandal, leading to his guilty plea, prison time (1996)

**William J. Jefferson (D-LA)**
Indicted in 2007 on 16 federal counts including bribery, racketeering, and money laundering. Convicted in 2009 on 11 counts related to accepting bribes (infamous for $90,000 found in his freezer). Sentenced to 13 years; some charges later overturned, released in 2017.
**Jesse Jackson Jr. (D-IL)**
Pleaded guilty in 2013 to wire fraud and conspiracy for misusing over $750,000 in campaign funds for personal expenses. Sentenced to 30 months in prison.
**Chaka Fattah (D-PA)**
Indicted and convicted in 2016 on 23 counts of racketeering, fraud, money laundering, and related charges involving misuse of campaign and charitable funds. Sentenced to 10 years in prison.
**Corrine Brown (D-FL)**
Indicted and convicted in 2017 on 18 felony counts of mail/wire fraud, tax evasion, and conspiracy related to a sham charity that diverted donations for personal use. Sentenced to 5 years; conviction initially overturned on appeal but she later pleaded guilty to tax fraud in a related matter.
**Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick (D-FL)**
Indicted in November 2025 on multiple federal counts (up to 17, including theft of government funds, money laundering, illegal campaign contributions, and tax fraud) for allegedly stealing $5 million in FEMA COVID-19 relief funds overpaid to a family company and funneling portions into her 2021/2022 congressional campaigns via straw donors. Case ongoing as of December 2025.
**Gregory Meeks (D-NY)**
Subject to FBI/DOJ investigation around 2010 for undisclosed loans, campaign finance issues, and potential nonprofit misuse in Queens politics. Subpoenaed; no charges filed.
"We, the People, recognize that we have responsibilities as well as rights; that our destinies are bound together; that a freedom which only asks what's in it for me, a freedom without a commitment to others, a freedom without love or charity or duty or patriotism, is unworthy of our founding ideals, and those who died in their defense."
**[Barack Obama](https://substack.com/redirect/f952ac8f-572c-430c-8004-4aef05b3895c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

name: NIGEL BRISTOW
subject: RE: Early Voting Starts Feb. 12 — Let’s Put People First Together
body:
Dear Friend,

Thank you for signing up and being part of our **People First** movement. Your support means more than you know — and right now, it truly matters.

**Early voting begins Thursday, February 12, and runs through Saturday, February 28 at 3:00 p.m.** Mark your calendar and bring someone with you. This early voting window will decide the outcome of this election.

I’m running for Congress because too many families in our district feel unseen and unheard — working people, seniors, veterans, students, and communities who just want a fair shot. This campaign is about restoring trust, protecting our rights, and making sure government works for people, not politics.

Here’s how you can help right now:

\- **Make a contribution** — even a small donation helps us reach voters with our message
\- **Volunteer** — phone banking, canvassing, or spreading the word online
\- **Vote early** and encourage **3 friends or family members** to do the same

Early voting is convenient, flexible, and powerful. When we show up early, we send a clear message: People come first.

If you’re able to [donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nigel-bristow-for-congress-1), [volunteer, or help get out the vote](https://www.wixforms.com/f/7424685363861390383), please click 'form' in the upper left of the voluteer link to take action today.

Thank you for believing in this campaign and in our community. Together, we can win — county by county, voter by voter.

With gratitude and determination,

Nigel Bristow
Candidate for U.S. Congress, NC-09
[nigelbristowforcongress.com](https://www.nigelbristowforcongress.com/)

Peter

We’re two and a half weeks into the 2026 legislative session, and the stakes couldn’t be higher.
While East Tennesseans struggle to afford groceries, medical care, utilities, and our neighbors are being snatched off the street by ICE, Republicans are wasting precious time on hate-filled legislation that divides us and does nothing to improve our quality of life.
Like you, I’m frustrated. We need real leadership and real solutions. We need people in office who understand that we deserve better than the divisive grandstanding that Tennessee MAGA Republicans are known for.
I’m fighting back in our state legislature – but we also need strong leaders from our state in D.C. that can take on the Trump administration, not bend over for it. That’s why I’m all IN for [Michaela Barnett](https://gmail.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=08ef345bf32fd78090e04097b&id=442a36958c&e=dc5f639d62), running for Congress in Tennessee’s District 2 against Tim Burchett. I’ve known Tim for a long time, and he does nothing for us in D.C. except embarrass us with his lack of knowledge and distaste for facts.
Michaela Barnett is a scientist, small business owner, and she spent the last year working in Congress, standing up to the Trump administration. Most of all, she’s a fighter. She knows firsthand what isn’t working in Washington, and I’m excited about her ideas and energy to help fix what’s broken.
I know better than most what it takes to fight the GOP establishment in TN, and that’s why I’m proud to endorse Michaela Barnett to be my Congresswoman! This race is going to take all of us. Michaela is our best chance to flip this seat to blue, and she needs our help.
Tim Burchett has corporate backers and the whole Republican establishment on his side. Michaela has me, you, and everyone else who believes that we deserve better in DC., each of us who believes that every human being in our community deserves respect and dignity. Can you help fuel her race?
Join me by clicking[ here to donate](https://gmail.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=08ef345bf32fd78090e04097b&id=cb17a72bb0&e=dc5f639d62) and/or going to [https://www.michaelafortennessee.com/ ](https://gmail.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=08ef345bf32fd78090e04097b&id=d6ad8c43d2&e=dc5f639d62)to sign up, learn more about Michaela, and to volunteer.
In solidarity,Gloria JohnsonState RepresentativeTennessee House District 90
